text: Found it: in src/plugin/timezone/index.js the static `dayjs.tz(input, tz)` always treats `input` as a wall-clock string (`d.utc(input).valueOf()`), so a Date/timestamp/Dayjs input gets re-interpreted as wall-clock in the target zone instead of being converted. Fix: delegate non-string inputs to the instance `tz()` conversion. Implementing and verifying now.

Working on it: the fractional-second offset looks like a rounding/truncation issue in the timezone plugin's offset computation (proto.tz / utcOffset path). Reproducing and pinning down the exact source now; I'll report back with the fix.
